title: November 19 — measuring through light, material from residue, sound from silence
summary: Six new repositories grow the curated census from 659 to 665: LightScan, FunWithOpticalLoops, 3 / THREE, PhaseLabyrinth, SplatYou and FireIntoSilence. Distinguishes physical optical validation from a convincing simulation, artistic frequency depth from 3D geometry, and musical feedback from neural novelty.

nodes.claim: A calibrated monitor–diffuser–phone optical inverse with held-out screen patterns and live 8×8 image reconstruction.
nodes.survived: The README describes black/white camera references, measured pattern responses, a regularized inverse and saved held-out reports.
nodes.killed: Real diffuser recovery of new text is not proven by a Gaussian-blur simulation; it is neither X-ray imaging nor 3D tomography.
nodes.era: November 19: measured light, residue and feedback music

nodes.claim: Browser WebGL cavity with simulated and physical webcam-to-monitor feedback modes.
nodes.survived: Homography lock, delay ring buffer, fractional rotation/zoom, auto-exposure ballast, kymograph and Poincaré diagnostics.
nodes.killed: Simulated regimes are not validation on real optics; camera exposure, rolling shutter and flicker constrain live results.
nodes.era: November 19: measured light, residue and feedback music

nodes.claim: THREE: three optical-art scenes built from greedy Gabor packets and coarse-to-fine residue.
nodes.survived: A standalone HTML demo of self-carving crystals, artistic frequency-as-depth layers and shatter/reform pieces.
nodes.killed: No calibrated 3D geometry or material depth; the fitter is hand-written and does not include trained SplatWorld weights.
nodes.era: November 19: measured light, residue and feedback music

nodes.claim: Five fade-triggered wave voices create corridors and feed a stereophonic musical delay labyrinth.
nodes.survived: Playable browser synthesizer, editable voices, feedback-cut and phase-freeze controls, Fourier petal editor and Takens scope.
nodes.killed: This is a designed dynamical instrument, not demonstrated biological learning or spontaneous understanding of music.
nodes.era: November 19: measured light, residue and feedback music

nodes.claim: SplatWorld's unchanged 7.2 MB ONNX face decoder meets frozen photo residue, optical inverse and semantic feedback.
nodes.survived: Residue Studio, active screen-mask probing and closed-loop camera innovation are implemented; synthetic numerical checks are documented.
nodes.killed: Actual diffuser inversion remains unvalidated; a face prior can invent a face for unrelated inputs and anchor details require a real photograph.
nodes.era: November 19: measured light, residue and feedback music

nodes.claim: Two fade-triggered wave units become a clockless and causally interruptible music instrument.
nodes.survived: Dependency-free browser field simulation, woven/dominant/silent presets, wave and event raster, feedback cut and MIDI output.
nodes.killed: Its engine is not bit-identical to the source Python and can settle into repeating rhythms; no learned beat or novel neural law is claimed.
nodes.era: November 19: measured light, residue and feedback music

edges.why: LightScan credits Moon as a compact inverse/forward-model influence, not a direct code port.
FireIntoSilence ports PerceptionLabAI's WaveFieldNode and FadingHistorySpikeNode mechanisms.
FireIntoSilence cites the fade-triggered GeometricNeuronV30 research thread.
PhaseLabyrinth explicitly builds on the fade-triggered voice mechanism in FireIntoSilence.
PhaseLabyrinth credits its cross-coupled stereo delay corridor design.
PhaseLabyrinth credits its live delay-embedding scope.
SplatYou embeds the unchanged original SplatWorld ONNX face decoder.
SplatYou cites weak-direction active sensing for screen mask selection.
SplatYou explicitly adopts the practical real-camera calibration discipline from LightScan.
THREE credits oriented splat primitives but runs a new untrained greedy image fitter.
THREE credits Moon's relightable design, with no physical BRDF calibration.

motifs.title: Calibrated physical transfer versus invented image content
motifs.description: LightScan measures an optical forward response; FunWithOpticalLoops feeds a camera back to the display; SplatYou restricts a camera inverse with a genuine face prior. All demand hardware controls.

motifs.title: Inhibitory wave memory can trigger an event when input fades
motifs.description: FireIntoSilence uses two fade-triggered units and PhaseLabyrinth expands the idea to five voices with delay feedback.

motifs.title: Residual details need a source, and stylized depth is not measured depth
motifs.description: THREE fashions Gabor residue into crystals; SplatYou borrows detail only from an immutable photograph. Neither recovers undisclosed 3D ground truth.
